title: SI Scholarship for Global Professionals
funding: Fully funded: monthly allowance and travel grant (subject to scholarship terms)
description: Fully funded master's in an English-taught programme in Sweden for professionals from eligible countries; includes a monthly allowance and travel grant.
requirements_text: Applicants must be citizens of an eligible country; have demonstrated work experience and leadership experience; apply to an eligible full-time master's programme in Sweden; and meet the programme's admission and English-language requirements. Applicants must also meet the applicable tuition-fee conditions. Check the official call for the exact eligible-country list, work-experience rules and current application requirements.

title: PhD in Computer Science
funding: Full tuition waiver, stipend and health insurance (confirm package and conditions with the department)
description: Doctoral programme in computer science for Fall 2027 entry. Priority deadline is 2026-12-01; final deadline is 2026-12-15.
requirements_text: Relevant academic background in computer science or a closely related field. Prepare academic transcripts, CV, statement of purpose and recommendation letters as required by the graduate application. English-proficiency requirements depend on the university's current policy and any applicable waiver. No universal minimum CGPA or IELTS score is entered here; verify the current official admissions requirements.

title: PhD in Data Science
funding: Tuition and fees, health insurance and stipend (subject to the programme's funding terms)
description: Doctoral programme in data science for Fall 2027 admission.
requirements_text: Applicants should have suitable preparation in a quantitative or computing field, including relevant mathematics, statistics and programming. Application materials generally include transcripts, CV, statement of purpose and letters of recommendation. IELTS 7.0 was previously identified as a recommended score, not a confirmed universal minimum; check the current NYU English-language policy and programme instructions before treating it as a cutoff.

title: PhD in Computer Science
funding: PhD financial support may include a stipend and tuition scholarship/waiver; support is competitive and subject to department terms
description: PhD in computer science for Fall 2027; the department notes that late applications are not possible.
requirements_text: Applicants need a relevant academic background and should submit academic transcripts, statement of purpose, CV and recommendation letters as specified by the department. International applicants must satisfy the university's English-proficiency rules unless exempt. Financial support and tuition-waiver consideration are subject to the department's current policies and deadlines. A 3.0 GPA figure should not be treated as a confirmed current programme cutoff without checking the official admissions page.

title: Computing PhD Studentships
funding: Fully funded PhD studentships; the department advertises up to 30 per year, subject to availability and selection
description: The Department of Computing offers fully funded PhD studentships to home and overseas students, awarded on academic excellence and research potential.
requirements_text: Applicants are normally expected to have a first-class bachelor's degree or a distinction-level master's degree (or equivalent) in a relevant scientific or technical discipline. Applicants must meet Imperial's English-language requirement at the level applicable to the programme. The exact accepted qualifications and IELTS component scores must be checked against the current official course and English-language pages.

title: PhD in Computer Science (Gates Cambridge and other trusts)
funding: Competitive funding through Gates Cambridge and other Cambridge Trust awards; funding is not automatic for every applicant
description: PhD in the Department of Computer Science and Technology; 2026-12-08 is the deadline for Gates Cambridge and other Cambridge Trust funding for applicants from most countries.
requirements_text: Applicants should have a strong academic record and meet the Department of Computer Science and Technology's PhD admission requirements. A research proposal, CV, transcripts, degree certificates and academic references may be required. Applicants should identify a suitable research area/supervisor and satisfy the University of Cambridge's English-language requirements. Funding applications have separate eligibility and deadline rules; check the relevant Gates Cambridge or Cambridge Trust scheme.

title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Data Engineering and Artificial Intelligence (DEAI)
provider: DEAI Consortium (coordinated by Université libre de Bruxelles)
field: Data Engineering; Artificial Intelligence; Computer Science
funding: Full scholarship: participation costs covered plus €1,400/month stipend; partial scholarship: participation costs covered without living stipend
description: Erasmus Mundus joint master's 2027–2029. Scholarship-track application deadline is 11 January 2027 at 12:00 GMT; reference letters are due 18 January 2027. Non-EU self-funded/partial-grant applications have a later deadline of 15 May 2027.
requirements_text: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree equivalent to 180 ECTS from an accredited university meeting the programme's stated recognition criteria. English proficiency at CEFR B2 is required; the official page lists IELTS Academic 5.5 as an example equivalent. Selection considers the bachelor's subject/Computer Science credits, academic results, other studies, professional experience, cover letter and reference letters. Scholarship awards are competitive and subject to final ranking.

title: Citizen-Centred Artificial Intelligence (CCAI) PhD
provider: Northumbria University / CCAI UKRI Centre for Doctoral Training
field: Artificial Intelligence; Human-Centred AI; AI Governance; Interdisciplinary Computing
funding: Fully funded: tuition fees, stipend and research training grant; international applicants welcome, funding at applicable UKRI rates
description: Four-year UKRI-funded PhD programme for September 2027 entry. Application deadline is 11 January 2027 at 17:00 GMT.
requirements_text: Open to applicants from technical, social-scientific, design, humanities, legal and professional backgrounds who want to research AI centred on citizens and communities. Applicants submit a two-page CV, research proposal, EDI data/optional personal statement, degree certificates and transcripts, and English-language evidence where required. International applicants are welcome; funding is at applicable UKRI rates. Check the programme's current international fee and stipend terms.

title: Funded PhD Studentship in Computer Science, IT and Software Engineering
field: Artificial Intelligence; Software Engineering; Interaction Design; Technology and Education; Multimedia and Networking
funding: Fully funded for 3 years and 3 months: course fees covered, stipend of at least £21,805/year, plus research training/support grant
description: Full-time PhD studentships starting 1 October 2027. International applicants are accepted. Applicants are expected to live in or near Milton Keynes and work on campus.
requirements_text: Applicants must hold an upper second-class honours degree or a master's degree in a relevant subject; overseas degrees are assessed under the UK ENIC framework. Non-UK/Irish applicants must demonstrate English-language competency. Application requires a project proposal, CV, degree certificates and proof of English competency where applicable. Applicants are strongly advised to identify a project and contact a potential supervisor before applying.

title: Computing Science PhD Studentships 2027
field: Computing Science; Healthcare Technologies; Cybersecurity; Data Science; Autonomous Systems; Programming Languages
funding: Studentships include tuition-fee support for home and international students; most include living expenses at UKRI stipend rate (£22,437 for 2027–28). Some international awards may be fee-discount rather than full international-fee coverage; verify award terms.
description: PhD studentships for research starting October 2027 or shortly thereafter. To be considered for the listed funding round, apply by 31 January 2027.
requirements_text: Normally requires an upper second-class honours undergraduate degree or equivalent, or a master's degree, in Computing Science or a related discipline. Applicants should identify a suitable project/supervisor and select 'Univ of Glasgow Scholarship' as the funding source in the application. Academic admission and scholarship consideration are separate; check each studentship's international-fee coverage and English-language requirements.

title: International Graduate Admission in Computer Science 2027
field: Computer Science and Technology; Artificial Intelligence (research areas subject to department catalogue)
funding: PhD students may apply for full financial support; Chinese Government Scholarship, Beijing Government Scholarship and Peking University scholarships may cover tuition, accommodation, living expenses and/or insurance depending on award. Not guaranteed.
description: 2027 international graduate admission in Computer Science. English-taught programme application period runs 26 October 2026 to 10 January 2027 (Beijing time).
requirements_text: Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport. Master's applicants need a bachelor's degree; PhD applicants normally need a master's degree, while bachelor's holders may apply directly to doctoral programmes in science and engineering. Academic performance and language ability must meet programme requirements. For English-taught programmes, non-native English speakers must submit IELTS above 6.5, TOEFL or other accepted evidence. Required materials include degree certificates, transcripts, a personal statement/research plan, CV, two recommendation letters and passport. Scholarships require separate application/review and are not guaranteed.

title: MSc Computing Science – Cyber Security and AI specialisation
field: Computer Science; Cyber Security; Artificial Intelligence
funding: Radboud Scholarship may be available for eligible non-EEA applicants; scholarship is competitive and not guaranteed. Scholarship deadline: 31 January 2027.
description: September 2027 intake. For applicants using the scholarship route, the programme page lists 31 January 2027 as the scholarship application deadline; the general admission deadline may be later depending on nationality and prior education.
requirements_text: Admission to the Master's in Computing Science is required for the Cyber Security and AI specialisation. The page lists a relevant research-university bachelor's degree in Computing Science or a related field such as AI/Mathematics, with additional requirements possible. Applicants need prior coursework in mathematics (including calculus, linear algebra, probability/statistics and related topics) and programming/algorithms. Exact admission period depends on nationality and previous education; select these on the official page. Apply by 31 January 2027 for Radboud Scholarship consideration where eligible.

title: Master in Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (September 2027 intake)
funding: Merit/other scholarships available on a rolling basis; €1,000 early application award for applications by 31 January 2027. Not a full scholarship.
description: September 2027 intake. Round three deadline is 31 January 2027 and carries a €1,000 early application award. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
requirements_text: Applicants must satisfy ESMT's academic and English-language admission requirements for the Master in Analytics and Artificial Intelligence. The admissions page describes rolling review and scholarships awarded on a rolling basis. The €1,000 award is a tuition reduction, not full funding. Check the programme's admission requirements and current scholarship criteria before applying.

title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Artificial Intelligence (EMAI) – self-funded application
country: Spain; Netherlands; Slovenia; Czech Republic (consortium mobility; confirm partner locations)
funding: Self-funded application period for worldwide applicants; no 2027 Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadline confirmed on the cited application page at time of checking.
description: 2027–2029 cohort. Worldwide self-funded candidates can apply from 25 November 2026 through 5 June 2027 at 23:59 CEST. EU self-funded second period runs 6 June to 6 July 2027.
requirements_text: Applicants should have relevant prior knowledge for the Artificial Intelligence joint master's. The programme may recognise formal and informal learning/experience through submitted certificates and a portfolio. The listed dates are for self-funded applicants; do not treat them as a confirmed scholarship deadline. Check the consortium's current admission and language requirements before applying.
